finding.expected: HTTP 200 with a body containing a string id.
finding.actual: HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"","path":"/groovy/submit","status":500}; body.id is undefined.

verdicts.rationale: A well-formed submission of `4+1+1` by an authenticated user returns 500 in 2ms with no id — the response is the service declaring its own fault, which no intent for a submit endpoint can sanction, so this is not drift. Caveat for the human: section 2022-test-plan/4.1.1 is absent from the intent dir, so I could not read the requirement text; the verdict rests on the 500 being self-evidently unintended rather than on a quoted line.

finding.title: POST /groovy/submit returns 500 Internal Server Error for a valid single-line groovy submission
finding.intent: 2022-test-plan/4.1.1 — section NOT FOUND in the intent dir; requirement inferred as "an authenticated user can submit single-line groovy code and receive an id"
finding.expected: 200 with body.id present as a string identifying the submission
finding.actual: 500 Internal Server Error after 2ms; body {"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"","path":"/groovy/submit","status":500,"timestamp":"2026-08-29T13:04:24.973Z"}; body.id absent

verdicts.rationale: Same failure signature as CASE-2022-4-1-1 — a conditional-statement submission returns 500 in 1ms with no id. The sub-millisecond latency indicates the request fails before any groovy is evaluated, so this is very likely the same root cause rather than a distinct defect in conditional handling; the human should treat the two as one fix. Section 2022-test-plan/4.1.4 is likewise absent from the intent dir.

finding.actual: 500 Internal Server Error after 1ms; body {"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"","path":"/groovy/submit","status":500,"timestamp":"2026-08-29T13:04:24.975Z"}; body.id absent

verdicts.rationale: This case asks whether a payload missing the `code` field is rejected with 400/422, but CASE-2022-4-1-1 shows that /groovy/submit answers 500 even for a well-formed body, so the observed 500 is not evidence about validation behavior — the case's actual claim was never exercised. Classifying it as a validation bug would file a second, probably phantom, defect on top of the blanket 500. Re-adjudicate once submit is serving again.
verdicts.prescription: Re-run CASE-2022-2-1 (seed 42) only after POST /groovy/submit returns 200 for the valid-body probe (CASE-2022-4-1-1). If it then still answers 500 rather than 400/422, the result is real evidence and should be re-triaged as a candidate bug; if it answers 422, that is a drift question against 2022-test-plan/2.1, which must be present in the intent dir before it can be adjudicated.

verdicts.rationale: The failure is in setup[0] — the submit that mints requestId returned 500, so no id was captured and the test request (user_2 reading user_1's status) never ran. Nothing was observed about the 401-vs-403 question this case exists to settle, so there is no evidence to distinguish bug from drift. Note this case is the pre-registered PR2 adjudication specimen (RFC 0001 §8), so it should not be silently retired on a blocked run.
verdicts.prescription: Re-run CASE-2022-1-5 (seed 42) after POST /groovy/submit is restored, so setup[0] captures body.id. Judge the resulting status on its own evidence against 2022-test-plan/1.5 — which must first be present in the intent dir, since the case notes flag a known 401/403 conflict with test-plan AC 1.4 that cannot be adjudicated without the intent text.

verdicts.rationale: The intent explicitly pins the refusal status: non-submitters must get 403 Forbidden. The service returned 401 Unauthorized for an authenticated principal (user_1) reading user_2's request, contradicting a detail the intent names outright. Deterministic across all 5 instances, so not nondeterminism; note the isolation property itself was not breached (no result was disclosed) — only the refusal code differs, and a 401 may indicate the second principal's credentials are rejected before authorization is ever evaluated, which would leave the invariant untested.

finding.title: Cross-user GET /groovy/status returns 401 Unauthorized instead of the required 403 Forbidden
finding.intent: result-isolation
finding.expected: GET /groovy/status for a request submitted by user_2, performed as user_1, returns 403 Forbidden
finding.actual: Returns 401 Unauthorized with body {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"","path":"/groovy/status","status":401}

verdicts.rationale: Same deterministic contradiction as the other instances in this family: the intent names 403 Forbidden for any principal other than the submitter, and the service answered 401 Unauthorized. The case does not over-specify here — the status is stated in the invariant line itself.
